summary: Add tag storage, mutation endpoints, query filtering, and response mapping so operators can organize alerts with free-form tags and filter by them.

acceptance_criteria.text: Persist tags for alerts through a new Tag concept with a many-to-many schema and migration.
POST /api/alerts/{id}/tags adds one or more tags, dedupes case-insensitively, limits each alert to 10 tags, and enforces 1-30 characters per tag.
DELETE /api/alerts/{id}/tags/{tag} removes a tag assignment and returns 404 when the alert or assignment does not exist.
GET /api/alerts supports an optional tag filter that composes with the existing isActive, severity, date range, search, sorting, and paging filters.

implementation_steps: 1. Update AlertConstants, AlertQueryRequest, AddAlertTagsRequest, and AlertResponse for tag limits, filter input, add-tags payload, and response shape.
2. Extend Alert, create Tag, and update AlertMappingExtensions so tags flow through the domain and DTO layers.
3. Extend IAlertRepository, IAlertService, and AlertManagementService with tag mutation operations and tag-aware query orchestration.
4. Update AlertsController to expose POST /api/alerts/{id}/tags and DELETE /api/alerts/{id}/tags/{tag} on the existing alert surface.
5. Update AlertDbContext, AlertConfiguration, TagConfiguration, and AlertRepository for the new many-to-many mapping, query filter, and persistence logic.
6. Create the AddAlertTagging migration, refresh AlertDbContextModelSnapshot, and regenerate database/02_AlertServiceDb_Migrations.sql.
7. Expand controller, service, and repository tests for tag validation, persistence, filtering, response mapping, and not-found behavior.

planned_tests.test: Repository tests persist tags and the AlertTags join rows, then reload alerts with their tag collection populated.
Controller and service tests add multiple tags to an alert and return the updated alert payload with deduped tags.
Request validation rejects null or empty tag payloads, blank values, and tags longer than 30 characters.
Service or controller tests reject a request that would leave the alert with more than 10 tags.
Repository or service tests treat differently cased duplicates as one tag assignment for the alert.
Controller and repository tests remove an existing tag assignment and confirm the alert no longer returns that tag.
Controller or service tests return not found when the alert is missing or the tag is not assigned to that alert.
Repository tests filter alerts by tag while still honoring severity, activity, date range, search, sorting, and paging.
Repository tests match the tag filter case-insensitively without changing existing paging totals.
Service and repository tests confirm AlertResponse includes tag names on list and single-alert reads.

contract_changes.api: GET /api/alerts gains the optional tag query filter, POST /api/alerts/{id}/tags and DELETE /api/alerts/{id}/tags/{tag} are added, and AlertResponse includes tags.
contract_changes.database: Add the Tags table, the AlertTags join table, related indexes, and the EF Core migration plus refreshed idempotent script.

boundaries.primary_slice: Alert tagging across the AlertsController, AlertManagementService, AlertRepository, and EF Core alert model.
out_of_scope: Dedicated tag administration endpoints outside the alert resource.
Changes to alert summary behavior or non-tag alert filters.

assumptions: Invalid tag additions return 400 with the existing API validation style instead of introducing a new error contract.
risks: Medium: the feature spans API, business rules, EF mapping, and query composition, so regressions can affect existing alert reads; rollback = revert the tagging files and migration.
Low: tag filtering must preserve paging and total counts when joins are introduced; rollback = remove the tag filter and eager-loading changes from the repository.
scope_override_reason: Alert tagging spans API, DTO, domain, repository, EF configuration, and generated migration artifacts, so it requires more than five production files.
